c.tagline: Where Geoffrey Bawa's gardens spill down to a golden river-mouth beach

taxi.color: Yellow-roofed three-wheelers (tuk-tuks) are the default ride; sedans and vans serve airport/long-distance transfers
taxi.fare: Roughly Rs. 100–150 (~$0.30–0.45) per km by tuk-tuk; a short hop within Bentota/Aluthgama runs $1–3
taxi.fareNote: Most tuk-tuks are unmetered — agree on a price before departure, or book through the PickMe app for a fixed, fairer metered fare

emergency.note: Tourist Police hotline: 1912. Fire & rescue: 110. Bentota has a small police post on Galle Road; the nearest hospitals with real capacity are in Aluthgama and Kalutara, with Colombo (National Hospital) roughly 1.5–2 hours away for serious cases.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

solo.f: Safety index is the main factor (71/100)

avoid.reason: Expect persistent 'beach boy' touts pushing tours and overpriced gem or spice-garden stops, and beware strong currents outside designated swimming areas.

hood_desc: The commercial heart of Bentota along the A2 (Galle Road), with the train station, shops, banks, and everyday restaurants — the natural base for exploring in every direction.
The river mouth and inland lake are where Bentota's boat safaris, mangrove tours, and Cinnamon Island cinnamon-processing demo depart from — lush, green, and much quieter than the beach.
The main resort strip south of the river mouth, lined with beachfront hotels from budget guesthouses to five-star resorts, plus most of the water sports operators.
A busier working town just across the Bentota River bridge, with a lively fish market, bus stand, and more local (non-resort) atmosphere and prices.
A low-key beach village a few kilometers south, best known for its turtle hatcheries and a calmer, less developed shoreline than central Bentota.

water.note: Stick to bottled or filtered water.

transit.hours: Trains run roughly 4:30am–9:30pm; buses along Galle Road run frequently from early morning until around 8–9pm.
transit.pay: Cash (LKR) for both trains and buses — fares are very cheap, typically $1–4 for train tickets and under $1 for local bus hops.
transit.map: Bentota Railway Station sits centrally on Galle Road; buses stop along the same road rather than at fixed shelters.
transit.note: Reserved observation-class or 1st-class seats are worth booking in advance for the scenic Colombo–Galle run; ordinary 2nd/3rd class carriages can be crowded but are an authentic, cheap way to travel.

train: Sri Lanka Railways' coastal line connects Colombo Fort to Bentota Railway Station in roughly 2–2.5 hours, continuing on to Galle and Matara
bus: SLTB and private intercity coaches from Colombo (Bastian Mawatha / Makumbura)

airport.name: Bandaranaike International Airport (Colombo)
airport.note: ~65 km / 1.5–2 hours by road. Pre-booked private taxi or hotel transfer ($25–45), PickMe app car, or a combination of the airport expressway bus/taxi plus the coastal train.

transit.m: Airport shuttle to Colombo Fort, then coastal-line train to Bentota (about 3 hr)

tip.s: Tipping isn't obligatory but is increasingly expected; Rs. 100–300 for tuk-tuk drivers, porters, spa therapists, and tour guides is appreciated.
tip.r: Many hotels and resorts already add a 10% service charge to the bill; if not included, leaving 10% in cash is standard at sit-down restaurants.

landmarks: Bentota Beach
A broad golden spit where the Bentota River meets the Indian Ocean, lined with palms and resorts, offering Sri Lanka's most polished stretch of southwest coast.
Lunuganga Estate
Legendary architect Geoffrey Bawa's country estate is a masterwork of tropical garden design, its terraces, lake vistas and artful follies open for guided visits.
Brief Garden
The whimsical home-garden of artist Bevis Bawa tumbles down a hillside in a riot of sculpture, courtyards and jungle greenery, delightfully eccentric and romantic.
Bentota River Safari
Boat trips glide through mangrove tunnels on the Bentota Ganga, spotting water monitors, crocodiles, kingfishers and troops of macaques minutes from the beach.
Kande Viharaya Temple
Home to one of the world's tallest seated Buddha statues at 48 meters, this hilltop temple near Aluthgama has drawn pilgrims since the eighteenth century.
Kosgoda Sea Turtle Hatchery
Conservation projects along Kosgoda beach protect eggs of five turtle species, letting visitors meet rescued turtles and watch hatchlings scramble to the sea.
Madu River and Cinnamon Island
A day-trip boat safari across Madu Ganga's mangrove-laced lagoon visits island temples and family cinnamon plantations demonstrating Ceylon's most famous spice.
Galapata Raja Maha Viharaya
This twelfth-century riverside temple, linked to King Parakramabahu's era, shelters ancient murals, a rock inscription and a serene bo tree away from the beach crowds.
Paradise Island Sandbar (Aluthgama)
A slender palm-fringed peninsula between river and ocean where fishermen haul nets at dawn, perfect for barefoot walks and postcard sunset photographs.
Ambalangoda Mask Museum
A short ride south, this workshop-museum preserves the lurid demon and healing masks of southern Sri Lanka's dance rituals, with carvers working before your eyes.

train.note: Bentota has its own small halt on the Coastal Line, but most useful trains stop instead at Aluthgama, about 2 km north across the river and a five-minute tuk-tuk ride away. Colombo Fort is roughly 2-2.5 hrs north and Galle about an hour south, with the track running right along the beach for much of the way. Most coastal services are unreserved, so tickets are bought at the counter on the day; the limited reserved seats on the intercity expresses can be booked through the Sri Lanka Railways seat reservation portal at seatreservation.railway.gov.lk or agents such as 12go.asia. There is no international rail from Sri Lanka - the ferry-linked service to India ended in the 1960s.

bus.note: Air-conditioned coaches on the old Galle Road between Colombo Fort and Galle stop in Bentota and Aluthgama and take about 2-2.5 hrs to Colombo for a few hundred rupees, while faster Southern Expressway highway buses do the run in around 90 minutes but use the Welipenna interchange several km inland. Services are a mix of state SLTB buses and private operators; there is no online booking and you simply pay the conductor on board. There are no international coach services from Sri Lanka, which has no land border.

ferry.note: Bentota has no scheduled passenger ferry - the boats you see on the Bentota Ganga are river safaris and watersports craft hired by the hour at the lagoon jetties near the road bridge. The nearest commercial passenger port is Colombo, about two hours north, and the country's only international sailing is the Nagapattinam-Kankesanthurai crossing far away in the north.

half.name: Hikkaduwa
half.blurb: A beach town with a protected coral reef visible by glass-bottom boat or snorkel, along with a lively surf break.

full.name: Udawalawe National Park
full.blurb: A dry-zone park built around a reservoir, known for reliable elephant sightings across its open grasslands.

notes.walk: The town itself is small and walkable along Galle Road and the beach strip, but Bentota, Aluthgama, and Induruwa are spread out over several kilometers, so tuk-tuks are the practical way to move between the beach, river, and town areas.
notes.card: Credit/debit cards are accepted at resorts, hotels, spas, and larger restaurants (Visa/Mastercard most common), but tuk-tuks, small eateries, roadside stalls, and the turtle hatcheries are cash-only, so carry LKR for daily spending.
notes.safety: Bentota is one of the more relaxed, tourist-friendly stretches of coast and is generally considered safe for solo travelers, including women, though normal precautions apply after dark on quiet beach paths. Violent crime against tourists is rare; the real risks are petty theft from unattended beach bags, overcharging by unlicensed tuk-tuk drivers and touts near the railway station, and occasional water-safety issues (rip currents) rather than crime.
notes.religion: Buddhism (majority, roughly 65–70%); Islam (~15%, historic Moor communities centered in nearby Aluthgama and Beruwala); Christianity (~10%, mostly Catholic, common along the southwest coast); Hinduism (~5%, largely Tamil estate and fishing communities)
notes.net: Dialog and Mobitel offer the strongest, most consistent 4G coverage along the south coast, including Bentota; Hutch and Airtel Lanka are usable backups. Wifi is standard in hotels, guesthouses, and beachfront cafes, though speeds can dip during peak season or storms. A tourist SIM or eSIM with 20–30GB typically costs $5–10, available at CMB airport arrivals or shops in Aluthgama/Bentota town. Most hotels and resorts include free wifi for guests; cafes generally offer it free with a purchase. A local SIM or eSIM (Dialog or Mobitel, bought at the airport or in Aluthgama/Bentota town) is recommended — hotel wifi is reliable, but a cheap prepaid data plan makes getting around by tuk-tuk and visiting turtle hatcheries or Lunuganga much easier.
notes.transit: No formal city transit; Sri Lanka Railways' coastal line (Colombo Fort–Galle–Matara) stops at Bentota Railway Station, and SLTB/private buses run the length of Galle Road (A2).
notes.transport: Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB) near Colombo is the main gateway, about 65 km / 1.5–2 hours north via the Southern Expressway; some visitors use seaplane or helicopter charters direct from CMB. Sri Lanka Railways' coastal line connects Colombo Fort to Bentota Railway Station in roughly 2–2.5 hours, continuing on to Galle and Matara. Frequent SLTB and private intercity buses run from Colombo (Bastian Mawatha/Makumbura) to Bentota along Galle Road or via the Southern Expressway, taking about 2 hours. No scheduled passenger ferries; small boats operate only for river and lagoon safaris on the Bentota River and Dedduwa Lake. Self-drive or hired car via the Southern Expressway (E01), exiting at the Welipenna or Aluthgama interchange, takes about 1.5 hours from Colombo.

laundry.note: Drop-off and guesthouse laundry; no published rates found
